Article summary

[Prev](https://support.6sense.com/docs/predictive-and-temperature-use-cases "Predictive and Temperature Use Cases")[Next](https://support.6sense.com/docs/account-profile-fit-model "Account Profile Fit Model")

Predictive intent scores predict the likelihood an account is interested in buying the product or service being sold. (Intent scores have also been called engagement scores.)

Predictive also uses intent scores to determine [buying stages (opens in new tab)](https://support.6sense.com/v1/docs/predictive-buying-stages) and [6QAs](https://support.6sense.com/v1/docs/6sense-qualified-accounts-6qas).

## Data inputs

The Predictive company activity AI model considers the following activities when calculating intent scores:

- CRM (excluding Task and Event)

- MAP

- Web

- Business-to-business network (B2BN) keyword

- 3rd party intent activities (using Bombora, G2, TrustRadius)


The intent score is the output of the Predictive company activity model that uses an account’s historical activity data to determine the likelihood of the account opening an opportunity in the next 90 days.

## How intent is measured

Intent is measured from 0-100, with a higher score indicating a higher interest, and therefore likelihood of opening an opportunity. Each account’s intent score is updated daily to account for any new activities.

## How intent is used

Intent scores are inputs to [buying stages (opens in new tab)](https://support.6sense.com/v1/docs/predictive-buying-stages) and [6QAs](https://support.6sense.com/v1/docs/6sense-qualified-accounts-6qas).

Also refer to the the Model Insights report, specifically the [Account behavior model](https://support.6sense.com/v1/docs/predictive-model-insights-report#account-behavior-model) panel that covers account buying stages.

      <!--
        d360-article Custom Element host-config.
        Set BEFORE the lazy stub so the CE bundle picks it up at bootstrap.
        `mermaidWrapAsImage: true` makes mermaid diagrams render as
        `<img data:image/svg+xml;…>` instead of inline `<svg>`. Site V2's
        host directive `appImageViewer` (viewerjs) then treats the diagram
        like an uploaded image — clicking opens the same lightbox.

        `tableFilterSortEnabledCheck` gates the table sort/filter header
        controls on the 'Table Sort & Filter' article setting. The CE reads
        this config object once at bundle load — before project metadata is
        available — so the closure reads the late-bound
        `__D360_TABLE_FILTER_SORT_ENABLED__` global (set by ProjectService
        from projectSetting.documentationSetting.articleContentSettings) at
        article-render time instead of capturing a value here.
      -->
      <script>
            window.__D360_ARTICLE_CONFIG__ = {

                  tableFilterSortEnabledCheck: function () {
                        return window.__D360_TABLE_FILTER_SORT_ENABLED__ === true;
                  },

      <!--
        D360_ARTICLE_CDN_INJECT marker.
        The Site V2 SSR pipeline (kb-site-angular-universal.module.ts)
        string-replaces this exact marker with a <script> tag that sets
        `window.__D360_ARTICLE_CDN__ = "${EDITOR360_URL}d360-article-element/main.js"`
        BEFORE the page is sent to the browser. The lazy stub below then
        picks up that global and fetches the CE bundle from the editor360
        CDN (same-origin localhost:5001 in dev, cdn.<env>.document360.net
        in qa/dev/staging/prod). If the marker is somehow not replaced
        (e.g. development without SSR pre-processing), the lazy stub
        falls back to the same-origin `/d360-article-ce/main.js` copied
        in by the gulp `copy-d360-article-ce` task.
      -->
      <link rel="preconnect" href="https://cdn.us.document360.io/" crossorigin=""><script>window.__D360_ARTICLE_CDN__ = "https://cdn.us.document360.io/static/mfe/editor360/d360-article-element/main.js";</script>
      <!--
        d360-article Custom Element lazy loader.
        Watches the DOM for a <d360-article> element and fetches the CE
        bundle on demand. Pages without an article (login, home, etc.)
        pay zero bytes.

        URL resolution (in priority order):
          1. window.__D360_ARTICLE_CDN__ — runtime override; set this from
             environment config (or any inline script BEFORE this stub) to
             point at the versioned CDN URL.
          2. Default `/d360-article-ce/main.js` — same-origin. The CE bundle
             is copied into Site V2's served output by the gulp
             `copy-d360-article-ce` task (see gulpfile.js + the
             `build:env:step3` script in package.json), which runs for BOTH
             local dev (`build:ssr-local`) and production (`build`). The
             namespace prefix `/d360-article-ce/` avoids colliding with
             Site V2's own root-level main.js / polyfills.js bundle names.

        SSR-safe: this <script> is preserved verbatim in the SSR output;
        Angular Universal does NOT execute inline scripts during render.
        The CE upgrade only fires in the browser. Article HTML reaches the
        CE via the `[attr.html]` attribute binding on <d360-article>
        (Angular serialises it as a real `html="..."` HTML attribute in
        the SSR output, which the CE wrapper's attributeChangedCallback
        picks up on upgrade).
      -->
      <script>
            (function () {
                  var loaded = false;
                  function load() {
                        if (loaded) return;
                        loaded = true;
                        // Resolve CE_URL HERE (not at IIFE invocation) so a value
                        // set by a LATER inline-script — e.g. the SSR-injected
                        // <script> for <!-- D360_ARTICLE_CDN_INJECT --> above us
                        // (executes first in head, so already set), or any future
                        // consumer that mounts main.ts before lazy-stub — is
                        // picked up. Defense-in-depth: keeps the stub safe even
                        // if the host changes the assignment timing.
                        var CE_URL = (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.__D360_ARTICLE_CDN__) || '/d360-article-ce/main.js';
                        // Polyfills (zone.js etc.) required by the CE bundle.
                        // Load before main so the CE bootstrap finds them ready.
                        var p = document.createElement('script');
                        p.src = CE_URL.replace(/main\.js$/, 'polyfills.js');
                        p.type = 'module';
                        p.defer = true;
                        document.head.appendChild(p);
                        var s = document.createElement('script');
                        s.src = CE_URL;
                        s.type = 'module';
                        s.defer = true;
                        document.head.appendChild(s);
                  }
                  if (document.querySelector('d360-article')) { load(); return; }
                  var obs = new MutationObserver(function () {
                        if (document.querySelector('d360-article')) { obs.disconnect(); load(); }
                  });
                  obs.observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });
            })();
      </script>

appfloikpreview="" appfiledownload="" ng-version="21.2.18" class="block-article editor360-published-content" html="<p data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-y16mpx-660">Predictive intent scores predict the likelihood an account is interested in buying the product or service being sold. (Intent scores have also been called engagement scores.) &nbsp;</p><p data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-y16mpx-660">Predictive also uses intent scores to determine <a href="/v1/docs/predictive-buying-stages" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">buying stages</a> and <a href="/v1/docs/6sense-qualified-accounts-6qas" rel="noopener">6QAs</a>. </p><h2 data-block-id="mcdcdwlx-mo1b29-682" id="data-inputs" class="hyperlink-wrapper-container">Data inputs<button class="copy-link-btn btn btn-secondary btn-icon" data-heading-id="data-inputs" aria-label="Copy link to Data inputs"><i class="fa-regular fa-link-horizontal"></i></button></h2><p data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-wnwfuu-663">The Predictive company activity AI model considers the following activities when calculating intent scores:</p><ul data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-jcbsad-664"><li data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-p8jv7y-665"><p data-block-id="mcdcdu4m-sw85ap-676"><span contenteditable="false" translate="no" data-glossary="CRM" data-glossary-name="CRM" id="blockglossary" class="fr-deletable popover__title" data-glossaryid="688ac102-ae03-4782-bdfd-e89813b814c6">CRM</span> (excluding Task and Event)</p></li><li data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-npi0wf-666"><p data-block-id="mcdcdu4m-qp4n7g-677"><span contenteditable="false" translate="no" data-glossary="MAP" data-glossary-name="MAP" id="blockglossary" class="fr-deletable popover__title" data-glossaryid="0bad413e-101c-40cd-ae5f-0fe319b15f7b">MAP</span></p></li><li data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-9syh79-667"><p data-block-id="mcdcdu4m-2nekj6-678">Web &nbsp;</p></li><li data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-uay6im-668"><p data-block-id="mcdcdu4m-9nrfkp-679">Business-to-business network (B2BN) keyword </p></li><li data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-pdlb94-669"><p data-block-id="mcdcdu4m-w5vuwq-680">3rd party intent activities (using Bombora, G2, TrustRadius)</p></li></ul><p data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-437kh9-670">The intent score is the output of the Predictive company activity model that uses an account’s historical activity data to determine the likelihood of the account opening an opportunity in the next 90 days. </p><h2 data-block-id="mcdcdu2i-uuk30u-671" id="how-intent-is-measured" class="hyperlink-wrapper-container">How intent is measured<button class="copy-link-btn btn btn-secondary btn-icon" measured from 0-100, with a higher score indicating a higher interest, and therefore likelihood of opening an opportunity.
